channel.title: EU & Swiss News Feed
channel.description: Latest news from Europe covering politics, economy, and security

item.title: [Politico Europe] Tusk government ‘facing armageddon’ as European court resumes cases against Poland
item.description: The country faces millions of euros in potential compensation payments over its former nationalist government’s judicial overhaul.

item.title: [Politico Europe] “Les COP, c’est une blague” : les critiques enflent contre les sommets climatiques après l’échec à Antalya
item.description: La fin chaotique de la COP31 pousse des pays à remettre en question tout le processus onusien de négociations climatiques.

item.title: [EU Observer] With no summit deal expected, it is clear the EU budget falls short on ambition – but does it matter?
item.description: After months of haggling and negotiation the next seven year EU budget looks devoid of ambition and purpose.

item.title: [DW] Peter Magyar meets Volodymyr Zelenskyy: Hungary and Ukraine make a fresh start after the icy relations of the Viktor Orban era
item.description: After years of frosty and hostile relations under Hungary's Kremlin-friendly former PM Viktor Orban, his successor, Peter Magyar, and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy seek to reset their countries' ties.

item.title: [Euractiv] LIVE: EU leaders to kick off budget battle royale
item.description: European leaders are in Brussels for a special two-day summit focused on the future long-term budget and Ukraine

item.title: [Euractiv] Midterms: Metsola’s fate uncertain as pro-EU coalition cracks
item.description: The pro-European alliance that keeps her in office is in trouble

item.title: [Politico Europe] Don’t ‘backslide’ on defense spending, senior US lawmaker tells Europe
item.description: Brendan Boyle said the EU needs to keep investing in defense amid fraught seven-year budget talks.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Exclusive] Details leaked of EU plan to cancel Russian sports in Europe, including Trump Jr.’s boxing pal
item.description: "Russia increasingly uses the fields of sports and culture as ... avenues for propaganda to legitimise its military aggression," said the draft EU sanctions text.

item.title: [Euractiv] EU delays planned AI gigafactories again
item.description: It’s at least the fifth setback the project has faced so far

item.title: [Euractiv] Kosovo’s Kurti wants EU to open up
item.description: Also, in tonight’s edition: EP midterm talks on ice, Slovenia goes after Kos, and Puigdemont returns to Spain

item.title: [Politico Europe] French presidential hopeful Teddy Riner says Ukraine is ‘not our war’
item.description: The Olympic gold medalist's remarks on Russia's ongoing full-scale invasion provoked a backlash.

item.title: [Euractiv] MEPs back an exposome moonshot, now national capitals must decide [Partner Content]
item.description: Parliament has written lifetime-exposure science into the next Horizon Europe programme, but its survival depends on governments that will want to see a return at home

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs want billions more to tackle migration in next seven-year EU budget
item.description: MEPs have demanded more than €3bn in additional funding for three key migration and home affairs programmes in the EU's next seven year budget.

item.title: [Euractiv] Proposed Global Europe cuts put EU’s external partnerships under pressure [Partner Content]
item.description: As EU governments negotiate the next long-term budget, proposed cuts to external action raise questions about the resilience and partnerships Europe depends on

item.title: [Euractiv] Can multilateralism be reinvigorated for the world’s complex crises? [Partner Content]
item.description: As the transatlantic partnership frays, multilateralism across the world is in decline. Rapporteur spoke with one group which is trying to revive it by looking at the specific ways it can tackle global crises like climate change

item.title: [EU Observer] Slovakia’s Fico snubbed Poland and Europe, insulted Ukraine veterans (again), and callously lied about Putin’s war (Ukraine Battlefield update, day 1,734)
item.description: As Slovak PM Robert Fico shrugs off war in Lviv and snubs both Warsaw and Brussels, thousands of grieving families, maimed soldiers and fresh Russian strikes in western Ukraine expose just how far his rhetoric has drifted from the front’s brutal reality.

item.title: [Euractiv] From steel to coffee: why Europe needs an integrated climate-trade strategy [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe’s climate and trade tools have not always been coordinated. From Italy’s low-carbon steel to its coffee imports and quality food exports, similar tensions recur. An integrated framework that rewards cleaner production is possible.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU commission proposes €50bn tech fund to buy into AI, quantum and other strategic companies
item.description: The EU Commission has presented plans to launch a €50bn tech sovereignty fund to take stakes in strategic companies to prevent them leaving to the US or China.

item.title: [EU Observer] EU court rules commission failed to act on citizens’ initiative calling for ban on animal cages
item.description: In the first ruling of its kind, the European Court of Justice decided that insufficient action was taken by the EU Commission after 1.4 million people signed an European Citizens’ Initiative petition to ban cages for farmed animals. The Brussels executive is expected to propose a cage phase-out plan in December.

item.title: [EU Observer] A Russian plan to federalise Moldova could give it a window to control access to EU membership
item.description: A reported Russian plan to federalise Moldova would hand the Kremlin a lever over who joins the EU. Europe should rule it out before it reaches the table.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘No woman is immune’ – AI ‘nudifiers’ that strip clothes from photos are thriving in Italian Telegram groups, report finds
item.description: Italian authorities, like Brussels, have been slow in combating anonymous online abuse targeting women through intimate photos. New research reveals just how quickly these groups reproduce.

item.title: [EU Observer] Listen: Can the United States actually dismantle the International Criminal Court?
item.description: Tajikistan has officially announced that it wants to leave the International Criminal Court. This comes as Donald Trump steps up his campaign against the court, with Washington threatening sanctions and putting diplomatic pressure on its allies. So, how serious is the threat to the ICC?

item.title: [EU Observer] Less EU money for farmers and regions, but a growing Ukraine bill: Leaders meet to square trillion-euro circles at special summit
item.description: EU leaders are heading for a clash over the bloc’s next long-term budget, with deep divisions over its size, new revenue sources and funding for Ukraine. German chancellor Friedrich Merz is demanding that all 27 member states contribute to Kyiv’s needs, while several countries are seeking opt-outs.

item.title: [EU Observer] [Interview] Cutting funds for Erasmus+ student scheme would be ‘giving up’ on Europe’s future, says lead MEP Zdrojewski
item.description: Students need not fear deep cuts to the Erasmus+ exchange scheme in the next EU budget, despite the frugal winds blowing from member states, says Bogdan Zdrojewski, a Polish MEP who is the EU Parliament's lead negotiator on the programme.

item.title: [ECFR] After Putin’s photo op, Europe must rejoin great-power diplomacy
item.description: The Shenzhen summit gave Putin recognition as an equal in a US-China-Russia format. But Europe should not mistake a vague declaration for a breakthrough, and it should insist on a seat at the diplomatic table

item.title: [EU Observer] Oil and gas firms join Big Tech push for faster EU data centre permits and weaker green rules
item.description: Eni, ExxonMobil and EDF are among the fossil-fuel firms that lobbied the European Commission to fast-track data centres, new research by Corporate Europe Observatory shows.

item.title: [ECFR] Fridges to fighter bases: The rise in Iranian hybrid attacks in Europe
item.description: Europe is facing a new direct threat to its homeland security coming from Iran. European governments must coordinate to disrupt and prevent future such threats

item.title: [ECFR] Cleaner together: Why energy cooperation is vital for a fossil-free Europe
item.description: Europe remains dependent on fossil fuels and has no clear phase-out goal. The EU’s six biggest states should unite through regional forums to lead Europe’s energy transition

item.title: [EU Observer] From strip searches to stillbirths: how Gaza’s women are being broken by Israel’s offensive
item.description: Israel's raging offensive in Gaza has meant most women have no access to a toilet. No hygiene, no sexual health, and frighteningly, no choice as to when to have a child - in breach of the Genocide Convention.

item.title: [EU Observer] ‘Null and void’: EU rejects Libya-Turkey pact that could allow oil drilling in Greek waters
item.description: The EU has flatly rejected a maritime deal between Turkey and Libya - but it poses a major headache for its relations with both countries.

item.title: [EU Observer] MEPs still split over ending Hungary’s Article 7 sanctions procedure, but Magyar’s reforms win praise
item.description: Unfreezing EU funds to encourage progress on the democratic reforms of the new Hungarian government were a good step, most MEPs said in a plenary debate, despite cries of ‘double standards’ from the right.

item.title: [DW] Ukraine's bid for NATO membership and more air defense remains controversial
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is calling for the rapid acceptance of his country into NATO. However, the necessary unanimity for this is lacking, as shown during the NATO Parliamentary Assembly in Berlin.

item.title: [DW] EU enlargement: Why do some EU member states use their vetoes to block the accession of certain candidate countries?
item.description: Individual EU member states use their veto powers to block candidate countries in the accession process — often for reasons of domestic politics. DW takes a look at some cases and examines what's behind them.

item.title: [ECFR] Networked nationalism: The global ambitions of Spain’s Vox party
item.description: Other Europeans should assume the far-right party would wield considerable foreign-policy influence in any Spanish government it joins

item.title: [ECFR] COP31 failed, but the green transition has not
item.description: COP31 ended without an overarching agreement, but Europe can still be a leader in the global green transition

item.title: [ECFR] Two prisoners, one rift: South Korea, Europe and Russia’s war on Ukraine
item.description: A spat over North Korean prisoners of war reveals a deeper divergence between South Korea and Europe over Russia. Shared ground rules can help their strategic partnership survive and thrive.

item.title: [Euractiv] Room to grow: acquisitions and Europe’s next tech champions [Promoted Content]
item.description: Europe struggles to scale its start-ups into global tech leaders. Drawing on new BRG research, the authors argue that, as the Commission finalises its merger guidelines, case-by-case assessment should weigh acquisitions’ risks against their role in helping European start-ups grow.

item.title: [DW] Can Rassvet, 'Russia's Starlink' change the course of the war in Ukraine?
item.description: SpaceX's US Starlink satellite system has played a key role in countering the Russian military in Ukraine, but now a Russian counterpart is under development. What could this mean for Ukraine in future?

item.description: Normalisation has not only put households on the hunt for returns but given them rapidly growing power to surprise markets

item.title: [DW] Putin proposes second humanitarian ceasefire — is it a trap?
item.description: Russian President Putin has suggested evacuating civilians from the embattled Ukrainian city of Kostiantynivka. But experts warn this could serve military, not humanitarian, aims. What should Kyiv do?

item.title: [ECFR] Choreographing a comeback: What Russia’s Africa policy means for Europe
item.description: The third Russia-Africa summit reflects Moscow’s global ambitions—coupling ideology with pragmatism beyond security partnerships. Europeans need to demonstrate that they are well-placed to back African-led projects and deliver reliable cooperation

item.title: [ECFR] The end of the exception: The future of Spain’s foreign policy
item.description: Spain’s coming election is likely to pave the way for a PP-Vox government. While this would end Madrid’s progressive exceptionalism, the PP’s ambition to bring Spain closer to Europe’s centre-right mainstream could be complicated by its prospective coalition partner

item.title: [DW] EU Commission confirms it was targeted in cyberattack using AI tools
item.description: The European Commission was targeted by an "AI-generated cybercampaign," a spokesperson has said. This is the first time the bloc has publicly reported an AI-based cyberattack.

item.title: [DW] Russian helicopter suspected of violating Finnish airspace
item.description: Finland's Defense Ministry thinks the incursion is linked to a drone strike earlier Saturday on a Russian cargo ship, which is on a US sanctions list.

item.title: [DW] EU and Indonesia sign trade deal
item.description: A deal covering 730 million people promises lower tariffs and new investment opportunities as the European Union seeks to diversify trade ties amid growing global economic tensions.

item.title: [DW] EU takes aim at tech giants in tax proposal
item.description: European Council President Antonio Costa has proposed a smaller EU budget for 2028-2034, including a 3% tax on major digital firms to ease member states' contributions. France has already rejected the plan as inadequate.

item.title: [DW] Russia strikes Zelenskyy's hometown, killing 2
item.description: The attacks follow Russian President Vladimir Putin's vow of a "painful" response to Ukraine's attacks this week on the Kerch Bridge, linking Russian-occupied Crimea.

item.title: [ECFR] Emergency Room: Inside the EU-UK reset deal
item.description: Mark Leonard and Jannike Wachowiak discuss EU-UK relations in this Emergency Room episode

item.title: [DW] North Macedonia remains stalled on its EU path after 21 years as a candidate
item.description: EU enlargement has regained momentum, with Montenegro and Albania moving closer to membership. But North Macedonia, a candidate since 2005, remains stalled by a politically difficult dispute involving Bulgaria.

item.title: [DW] German police respond to multiple school bomb threats
item.description: Police in Germany are responding to bomb threats against a series of schools, but say that at present they don't believe them to be credible. Danish authorities are reporting a similar series of apparent hoaxes.

item.title: [ECFR] Rearming without China: Time to secure Europe’s military supply chains
item.description: Europe’s militaries rely on Chinese supply. At the Foreign Affairs Council, ministers should agree to strengthen Asian partnerships and protect efforts to diversify mineral supply chains

item.title: [DW] Russian ornithologist jailed over small donations to Navalny's foundation
item.description: Sofia Rosenfeld has devoted her life to studying Arctic birds. A Russian court sentenced her to 3.5 years in a penal colony over donations to Navalny's foundation. Friends and family are fighting for her release.

item.title: [ECFR] Western Balkans: This political tsunami could change the region
item.description: Jessica Hendrick welcomes Milica Delević and Vladimir Petrović to discuss the landslide election that stunned Serbia

item.title: [ECFR] Investment at home, cooperation in Europe: How Italy can deal with hybrid threats
item.description: Italy is lagging in Europe when it comes to handling hybrid threats. Here is what it should do

item.title: [DW] EU and UK strike 'landmark deal' to strengthen ties after Brexit
item.description: The European Union and the United Kingdom have agreed on "landmark" deals on youth mobility and trade. Leaders on both sides praised the agreement as they seek to rebuild ties.

item.title: [DW] Turkey takes control of opposition broadcaster Sozcu TV
item.description: In the latest in a series of raids and arrests, another major pro-opposition Turkish broadcaster has been brought under state control. This is the third in a year.

item.title: [ECFR] Europe’s security after Abu Dhabi
item.description: Mark Leonard welcomes Wolfgang Ischinger and Jana Kobzová to discuss what the Abu Dhabi negotiations between the US, Russia and Ukraine mean for Europe’s security

item.title: [ECFR] After Abu Dhabi: How Europeans must reframe the European security debate
item.description: Russia has been allowed to frame the negotiations debate away from the need for a ceasefire in Ukraine. Here is how Europeans can shift the discussion back

item.title: [ECFR] More than Ukraine: How the Abu Dhabi talks laid bare Russia’s priorities
item.description: The talks in Abu Dhabi showed that Russia wants more than a deal on Ukraine: it wants to roll back the last 35 years of Europe’s security order. Europeans must not let this objective become the price of peace in Ukraine
